NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:20409  1   IN THE HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH
AT GWALIOR

BEFORE  HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE HIRDESH  ON THE 3 rd OF SEPTEMBER, 2025  MISC. APPEAL No. 7869 of 2023  NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LTD.
 Versus  SOMTA DEVI AND OTHERS  Appearance:
 Shri Kamal Kumar Rochlani - Advocate for the appella  Company.
 Shri Akhlesh Kumar Gupta, learned counsel for the re  to 6.
 ORDER

This is an appeal filed by the Insurance Company u/S 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 being aggrieved by the award dated 21.09.2023 passed by Member, Motor Claims Tribunal, Lahar District Bhind [in short "Claims Tribunal"] in MACC No.41/2023 seeking reduction of compensation amount awarded by the Claims Tribunal in favour of respondent Nos.1 to 6/Claimants.

entities.text: Motor Claims Tribunal, Lahar District Bhind
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. The date of accident, negligence and the issue of liability are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal in this regard are not in question.
3.

As per findings of the Claims Tribunal, in the case of death of Roop NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:20409 2 MA-7869-2023 Singh @ Malu, an amount of compensation to the tune of Rs.17,55,000/- has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal with interest in favour of claimants from filing of claim petition till its realization.
4. Learned counsel for appellant/Insurance Company submitted that award of the Claims Tribunal is against the fact, material available on record and against the settled principle of law.

It is further submitted that the Claims Tribunal has erred in assessing the income of the deceased on higher side National Insurance Company Ltd. vs Somta Devi on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133069399/
1 as the claimants have not produced and substantial as well as documentary evidence in regard to the income of the deceased.

sentences.text: Hence, it is prayed that compensation amount be reduced and just and reasonable amount of compensation may be awarded.
5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the claimants supported the impugned award passed by the Claims Tribunal and prayed for dismissal of this appeal.

6. Heard the arguments advanced by the counsel for the parties and perused the record of the Claims Tribunal.
7.

After hearing counsel for the parties, it is found that Claims Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased is on higher side as the claimants have failed to produce any cogent and substantial evidence in regard to income of the deceased.
Considering the evidence adduced by the Claims Tribunal and in considered opinion of this Court, deceased was not a skilled labour and claimants have not produced any income certificate
, therefore, the income of the deceased must be assessed as per Minimum Wages Act.

Hence, the just and proper amount of the income of the deceased NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:20409 3 MA-7869-2023 in the present case as per Minimum Wages Act is Rs.9,125/- per month instead of Rs.15,000/- per month.
8.

As regard to loss of income including future prospects, in the light of judgment of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi , 2017 ACJ 2700, the claimants are entitled for loss of income including future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi , 2017 ACJ 2700
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per Pranay Sethi (supra) , age of the deceased at the time of alleged accident was 55 years, therefore, future prospects be added at 10%.

Further, as per the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma and ors. Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr.
reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 , even if age of the deceased is to be taken into account, multiplier of 11 is to be applied.

entities.text:

reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
9. Accordingly, respondent Nos.1 to 6 - claimants are entitled to get compensation under the following heads:-
 HEAD AMOU  Income Rs.9,125/- pm  Future Prospects@10% (Rs.9125/- +912.5  Dependency 1/4 Rs.7528/-
 Annual Income Rs.7528 x 12= 90,
 Loss of Income Rs.90,338 X 11= 9  Other Heads:-
 Loss of Consortium Rs.40,000 X 6 = R Loss of Estate and funeral expenses Rs.30,000/-
Total = Rs.12,63,718/-
10.
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.12,63,718/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.17,55,000/-.

Accordingly, the compensation amount is reduced from Rs.17,55,000/- to Rs.12,63,718/-.
11.
In the result, the appeal is partly allowed by reducing the compensation amount to a sum of Rs.12,63,718/-..
The said amount shall bear interest @ 6 per cent from the date of the filing of the claim petition till its realization.
All other findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.
Insurance Company is entitled to get excessive amount (if already deposited) from the Claims Tribunal in accordance with law.
With the aforesaid modification, the appeal is partly allowed and stands disposed of.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE *VJ*
